text: Are we all sheep and what to do if other people can easily influence your opinions? I got this question from a young viewer who wrote Hello, I'm a young fan of your work and I really love your content. So can I ask a question and get your advice? So I'm a young student and I cannot form my own opinion and I have always thought I was open minded, but I am so easily influenced by others opinions and my TikTok feed that I am starting to wonder if I'm like sheep. Can I ask on how to avoid this and become a better listener and responder? Can you help? First, since the question was addressed to me, I'll just give you my personal opinion. This is by no means some ultimate truth. You are completely free to agree or disagree with me. But what I actually think is that to some extent, we're all sheep. And the biggest problem when you are young is that you rarely get to choose your shepherds. You don't choose your family, where you are born, the culture you grow up in or most of the people surrounding you. All of that shapes how you see the world before you are even old enough to question it. But as you get older and become more independent, something changes. You can start choosing your shepherds. And by shepherds, I just mean people or even fictional characters whose qualities you admire and whose example influences the direction you go in. I was quite lucky here. I had strong male figures growing up. My grandfather, my dad and my older brother certainly weren't perfect, but overall, they had a very positive influence on my upbringing. I also grew up reading quite a bit. So some of my role models weren't even real people. One of my favorite books was Captain Blood by Raphael Sabatini. And I really like characters like Aragorn from The Lord of the Rings. Looking back now with a little more life experience, I realize that some of those characters are almost too ideal. These days, I normally find flawed characters more interesting. Someone like Tyrion Lannister feels much more human to me, because realistically, very few people are going to be as consistently righteous as someone like Ned Stark. And with real people, I tend to look up to a more intelligent, older people who had a lot of life experience. I work in finance, so I really like Charlie Bunger. I studied economics, so I enjoy listening to Thomas Sow. So in that sense, I'm still a sheep, too. I am influenced by other people just like you are. I just try to be careful about choosing which people I allow to influence me. And that's probably the main advice I would give you. There's nothing wrong with watching TikTok, YouTube videos or listening to other people's opinions. You are supposed to be influenced by new information. Changing your mind isn't exactly a weakness. The important part is learning to question what is influencing you. If you notice yourself suddenly moving very strongly in one direction, especially towards something radical, question it even harder. Ask yourself, why do I believe this? What evidence would convince me that I'm wrong? What evidence actually supports this claim? And then check it. That also means learning some basic statistics, mathematics and logic, because otherwise it becomes very easy for someone to show you one impressive looking number and make you believe almost anything. And it's a gradual process. Nobody suddenly wakes up one morning with perfectly independent opinions. The fact that you are young and you are already questioning your own beliefs and how easily you can be influenced is actually a very good start. So I wouldn't be afraid of being a sheep. To some extent, all of us are. Be afraid of blindly following the wrong shepherd.
